title: Icy Moons
description: Far from the Sun there should be nothing but ice, yet Europa and Enceladus hide oceans. Their planets keep flexing them: an eccentric orbit brings a moon nearer and farther each turn, so its tidal bulge rises and falls, and the ice rubs itself warm. How warm depends on how the ice yields, which a lab measures by squeezing it in cycles. Cassini flew through Enceladus's plumes and found grains of silica, which form only where hot water meets rock. Unlocks the Ice Rheometer; the Plume Field lies in the Titan Ocean.

puzzle.goal: A moon of radius R at distance a from a planet of mass M feels a stronger pull on its near side than its far side. For R much less than a, write the difference Δg in the planet's acceleration across the moon, with G the gravitational constant.
puzzle.name: Tidal acceleration
puzzle.ask: Find Δg in m/s² for Saturn (M = 5.68e26 kg) acting across Enceladus (R = 2.52e5 m) at a = @{a} m, G = 6.674e-11.
puzzle.method: GM/(d − R)² − GM/(d + R)² ≈ GM·4R/d³ across the diameter, 2GMR/d³ from centre to surface: the derivative of 1/d² adds a power.
